title: Thy Ceaseless, Unexhausted Love
description: Thy Ceaseless, Unexhausted Love in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 250.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy cease-less, un-ex-haust-ed love, Un-mer-it-ed and free, De-lights our e-vil to re-move, And help our mis-e-ry.

lines: Thou waitest to be gracious still;
That, saved, we may thy goodness feel,
Thy goodness and thy truth to me,
Where all our thoughts are drowned.
Its streams the whole creation reach,
Enough for all, enough for each,
Faithful, O Lord, thy mercies are,
And while the truth of God remains,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
